stories.title: 📜 Baruch 1
summaryBullets: These are the words of the book that Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah son of Zedekiah son of Hasadiah son of Hilkiah wrote in Babylon, (1:1).
in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans took Jerusalem and burned it with fire. (1:2).
Baruch read the words of this book to Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and to all the people who came to hear the book (1:3).
and to the nobles and the princes and to the elders and to all the people, small and great, all who lived in Babylon by the River Sud. (1:4).
Then they wept and fasted and prayed before the Lord; (1:5).
they collected as much silver as each could give (1:6).
and sent it to Jerusalem to the priest Jehoiakim son of Hilkiah son of Shallum the priest and to the priests and to all the people who were present with him in Jerusalem. (1:7).

At the same time, on the tenth day of Sivan, Baruch took the vessels of the house of the Lord that had been carried away from the temple, to return them to the land of Judah—the silver vessels that Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made (1:8).
after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had carried away from Jerusalem Jeconiah and the princes and the prisoners and the nobles and the people of the land and brought them to Babylon. (1:9).

They said, “Here we send you silver, so buy with the silver burnt offerings and for purification offering and incense, and prepare a grain offering, and offer them on the altar of the Lord our God, (1:10).
and pray for the life of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and for the life of his son Belshazzar, so that their days on earth may be like the days of heaven. (1:11).

The Lord will give us strength and light to our eyes; we shall live under the protection of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and under the protection of his son Belshazzar, and we shall serve them many days and find favor in their sight. (1:12).
Pray also for us to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and to this day the anger of the Lord and his wrath have not turned away from us. (1:13).
And you shall read aloud this scroll that we are sending you, to make your confession in the house of the Lord on the days of the festivals and at appointed seasons. (1:14).
“And you shall say: To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us, this day, public shame, on the people of Judah, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, (1:15).
and on our kings, our rulers, our priests, our prophets, and our ancestors, (1:16).
because we have sinned before the Lord. (1:17).
We have disobeyed him and have not heeded the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in the statutes of the Lord that he set before us. (1:18).
From the time when the Lord brought our ancestors out of the land of Egypt until today, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God, and we have been negligent in not listening to his voice. (1:19).

So to this day there have clung to us the calamities and the curse that the Lord declared through his servant Moses at the time when he brought our ancestors out of the land of Egypt to give to us a land flowing with milk and honey. (1:20).
We did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God in all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us, (1:21).
but all of us followed the intent of our own wicked hearts by serving other gods and doing what is evil in the sight of the Lord our God. (1:22).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 36:4: Baruch son of Neriah writes down on a scroll the words dictated to him.
2 Kings 24:12-16: Nebuchadnezzar carries Jehoiachin, the officials, and the temple treasures to Babylon.
Jeremiah 29:4-7: The exiles are told to pray for the welfare of the city they were carried to.
Ezra 1:7-11: The vessels of the house of the Lord taken from Jerusalem are counted out again.
Nehemiah 9:32-34: Kings, officials, priests, and ancestors alike are named in a confession of disobedience.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ἐπὶ ποταμοῦ Σουδ (epi potamou Soud)
translationNotes.note: The exiles gathered at a watercourse in Babylonia. Lower Mesopotamia was crossed by large irrigation canals, and both Greek and Hebrew call such canals rivers, as with the Chebar in Ezekiel 1:1.
The third month of the Hebrew calendar, falling across May and June. The month names used after the exile, Sivan among them, came into Hebrew from Babylonian usage.

translationNotes.original: Greek: ὁλοκαύτωμα (holokautoma) - περὶ ἁμαρτίας (peri hamartias) - λίβανος (libanos)
translationNotes.note: Three separate items of temple worship, not synonyms. The burnt offering was consumed whole by fire, the purification offering dealt with defilement, and libanos is frankincense, a tree resin burned for its smoke.

translationNotes.term: Vessels of the house of the Lord
translationNotes.original: Greek: τὰ σκεύη οἴκου κυρίου (ta skeue oikou kyriou)
translationNotes.note: Not furniture but the working service equipment of the temple: basins, bowls, cups, snuffers, and censers of silver and gold. Such items were inventoried by weight and carried off in the deportations.

stories.keyTakeaway: Baruch reads his book in Babylon to King Jeconiah and the exiles by the River Sud; they weep, fast, and send silver and the temple vessels to Jerusalem for offerings, asking prayer for Nebuchadnezzar and Belshazzar and enclosing a confession that Judah has disobeyed since Egypt.

stories.title: 📜 Baruch 2
summaryBullets: “So the Lord carried out the threat he spoke against us: against our judges who ruled Israel and against our kings and our rulers and the people of Israel and Judah. (2:1).
Under the whole heaven there has not been done the like of what he has done in Jerusalem, in accordance with what is written in the law of Moses, (2:2).
that we would each eat the flesh of our sons and the flesh of our daughters. (2:3).
He made them subject to all the kingdoms around us, to be an object of scorn and a desolation among all the surrounding peoples, where the Lord has scattered them. (2:4).
They were brought down and not raised up, because we sinned against the Lord our God and did not listen to his voice. (2:5).
“To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us, this day, open shame. (2:6).
All those calamities with which the Lord threatened us have come upon us. (2:7).
Yet we have not entreated the favor of the Lord by turning away, each of us, from the thoughts of our wicked hearts. (2:8).
And the Lord has kept the calamities ready, and the Lord has brought them upon us, for the Lord is just in all the works that he has commanded us to do. (2:9).
Yet we have not obeyed his voice, to walk in the statutes of the Lord that he set before us. (2:10).

“And now, O Lord God of Israel, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and with signs and wonders and with great power and outstretched arm and made yourself a name that continues to this day, (2:11).
we have sinned, we have been ungodly, we have done wrong, O Lord our God, against all your ordinances. (2:12).
Let your anger turn away from us, for we are left few in number among the nations where you have scattered us. (2:13).
Hear, O Lord, our prayer and our entreaty, and for your own sake deliver us and grant us favor in the sight of those who have carried us into exile, (2:14).
so that all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God, for Israel and his descendants are called by your name. (2:15).
“O Lord, look down from your holy dwelling and consider us. Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear; (2:16).
open your eyes, O Lord, and see, for the dead who are in Hades, whose spirit has been taken from their bodies, will not ascribe glory or justice to the Lord, (2:17).
but the person who is deeply grieved, who walks bowed and feeble, with failing eyes and famished soul, will declare your glory and righteousness, O Lord. (2:18).
“For it is not because of any righteous deeds of our ancestors or our kings that we bring before you our prayer for mercy, O Lord our God. (2:19).
For you have sent your anger and your wrath upon us, as you declared by your servants the prophets, saying: (2:20).
‘Thus says the Lord: Bend your shoulders and serve the king of Babylon, and you will remain in the land that I gave to your ancestors. (2:21).
But if you will not obey the voice of the Lord and will not serve the king of Babylon, (2:22).

I will silence from the towns of Judah and from the region around Jerusalem the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, and the whole land will be a desolation without inhabitants.’ (2:23).

“But we did not obey your voice to serve the king of Babylon, and you have carried out your threats that you spoke by your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our ancestors would be brought out of their resting place, (2:24).
and indeed they have been thrown out to the heat of day and the frost of night. They perished in great misery, by famine and sword and pestilence. (2:25).
And the house that is called by your name you have made as it is today because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah. (2:26).
“Yet you have dealt with us, O Lord our God, in all your kindness and in all your great compassion, (2:27).
as you spoke by your servant Moses on the day when you commanded him to write your law in the presence of the people of Israel, saying, (2:28).
‘If you will not obey my voice, this very great multitude will surely turn into a small number among the nations, where I will scatter them. (2:29).
For I know that they will not obey me, for they are a stiff-necked people. But in the land of their exile they will have a change of heart (2:30).
and know that I am the Lord their God. I will give them a heart that obeys and ears that hear; (2:31).
they will praise me in the land of their exile and will remember my name (2:32).
and turn from their stubbornness and their wicked deeds, for they will remember the ways of their ancestors, who sinned before the Lord. (2:33).

I will bring them again into the land that I swore to give to their ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they will rule over it, and I will increase them, and they will not be diminished. (2:34).
I will make an everlasting covenant with them to be their God, and they shall be my people, and I will never again remove my people Israel from the land that I have given them.’ (2:35).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 28:53: The siege curse of the law, that parents would eat their own children.
Jeremiah 27:11-12: Bring your neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and remain in your own land.
Jeremiah 16:9: The Lord silences the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.
Jeremiah 8:1-2: The bones of Judah's kings brought out of their graves and spread before the sun.
Deuteronomy 30:1-5: In the land of exile Israel turns back, and the Lord gathers them to the land of their ancestors.

translationNotes.note: In the Greek Old Testament Hades is the standard rendering of the Hebrew Sheol: the grave, the common place of the dead. It is not the sorted underworld of reward and punishment that the same word names in Greek poetry.
A plowing image. An ox that will not turn its neck under the driver's hand is stiff-necked. Applied to people it means refusing to be steered, not simply being proud.

translationNotes.term: The voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride
translationNotes.original: Greek: φωνὴ νυμφίου καὶ φωνὴ νύμφης (phone nymphiou kai phone nymphes)
translationNotes.note: Weddings in that world were a public procession with singing through the streets. The silence of those two voices is a standing biblical shorthand for a town emptied of its people.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּרִית עוֹלָם (berit olam) - Greek: διαθήκη αἰώνιος (diatheke aionios)
translationNotes.note: In ordinary Greek a diatheke is a will or testament. The translators used it for the Hebrew berit, a binding agreement sworn between two parties and carrying obligations on both sides.

stories.keyTakeaway: The confession continues. The exiles admit the Lord did to Jerusalem what the law of Moses threatened, down to parents eating their children, and plead for mercy for his own name's sake, recalling his promise to give them a heart that obeys and bring them home under an everlasting covenant.

stories.title: 📜 Baruch 3
summaryBullets: “O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, the soul in anguish and the wearied spirit cry out to you. (3:1).
Hear, O Lord, and have mercy, for we have sinned before you. (3:2).
For you are enthroned forever, and we are perishing forever. (3:3).

O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear now the prayer of those of Israel who have died and of the children of those who sinned before you, who did not heed the voice of the Lord their God, so that calamities have clung to us. (3:4).
Do not remember the iniquities of our ancestors, but in this crisis remember your power and your name. (3:5).
For you are the Lord our God, and it is you, O Lord, whom we will praise. (3:6).

For you have put the fear of you in our hearts so that we would call upon your name, and we will praise you in our exile, for we have put away from our hearts all the iniquity of our ancestors who sinned against you. (3:7).
See, we are today in our exile where you have scattered us, to be reproached and cursed and punished for all the iniquities of our ancestors, who forsook the Lord our God.” (3:8).
Hear, O Israel, the commandments of life; give ear and learn wisdom! (3:9).
Why is it, O Israel, why is it that you are in the land of your enemies, that you are growing old in a foreign land, (3:10).
that you are defiled with the dead, that you are counted among those in Hades? (3:11).
You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom. (3:12).
If you had walked in the way of God, you would be living in peace forever. (3:13).

Learn where there is wisdom, where there is strength, where there is understanding, so that you may at the same time discern where there is length of days and life, where there is light for the eyes and peace. (3:14).
Who has found her place, and who has entered her storehouses? (3:15).
Where are the rulers of the nations and those who lorded it over the animals on earth; (3:16).
those who made sport of the birds of the air and who hoarded up silver and gold in which people trust, and there is no end to their getting; (3:17).
those who schemed to get silver and were anxious, but there is no trace of their works? (3:18).
They have vanished and gone down to Hades, and others have arisen in their place. (3:19).
Younger people have seen the light of day and have lived upon the earth, but they have not learned the way to knowledge, nor understood her paths, nor laid hold of her. (3:20).
Their descendants have strayed far from their way. (3:21).
She has not been heard of in Canaan or seen in Teman; (3:22).

the descendants of Hagar, who seek for understanding on the earth, the merchants of Merran and Teman, the storytellers and the seekers for understanding, have not learned the way to wisdom or given thought to her paths. (3:23).
O Israel, how great is the house of God, how vast the territory that he possesses! (3:24).
It is great and has no bounds; it is high and immeasurable. (3:25).
The giants were born there, who were famous of old, great in stature, expert in war. (3:26).
God did not choose them or give them the way to knowledge, (3:27).
so they perished because they had no wisdom; they perished through their folly. (3:28).
Who has gone up into heaven and taken her and brought her down from the clouds? (3:29).
Who has gone over the sea and found her and will buy her for pure gold? (3:30).
No one knows the way to her or is concerned about the path to her. (3:31).
But the one who knows all things knows her; he found her by his understanding. The one who prepared the earth for all time filled it with four-footed creatures; (3:32).
the one who sends forth the light and it goes, he called it, and it obeyed him, trembling; (3:33).
the stars shone in their watches and were glad; (3:34).
he called them, and they said, “Here we are!” They shone with gladness for him who made them. (3:35).
This is our God; no other can be compared to him. (3:36).
He found the whole way to knowledge and gave her to his servant Jacob and to Israel, whom he loved. (3:37).
Afterward she appeared on earth and lived with humankind. (3:38).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 30:11-14: The commandment is not in heaven or across the sea that someone must go and fetch it.
Job 28:12-23: Where is wisdom found? God alone understands the way to her.
Genesis 6:4: The giants on the earth in those days, the mighty men of old, men of renown.
Isaiah 40:26: God brings out the host of the stars by number and calls each one by name.
Deuteronomy 4:5-8: Israel's statutes are her wisdom in the sight of the nations.

translationNotes.note: The Greek translators rendered the Hebrew nephilim of Genesis 6 with gigantes, the word Greek mythology used for the kin of the Titans. That pagan vocabulary is the loan; the reference is to the mighty men of old named in Genesis.
A district of Edom, southeast of Judah, and a byword for wise men. That reputation is why Jeremiah 49:7 asks whether wisdom has vanished from Teman.
Literally the tellers of tales. Baruch lists them beside the caravan merchants as a trade: people who dealt in lore and story for a living, not authors of fiction in the modern sense.
Sophia is a grammatically feminine noun, so every pronoun attached to it in Greek is feminine. English translations keep her and she because the Greek grammar requires it.

stories.keyTakeaway: The prayer ends asking God to remember his own name, not the ancestors' guilt. A poem then asks why Israel grows old in a foreign land and answers that she forsook the fountain of wisdom; rulers, merchants, and the giants of old perished without her. God alone knows her way, and gave her to Jacob.

stories.title: 📜 Baruch 4
summaryBullets: She is the book of the commandments of God, the law that endures forever. All who hold her fast will live, and those who forsake her will die. (4:1).
Turn, O Jacob, and take her; walk toward the shining of her light. (4:2).
Do not give your glory to another or your advantages to a foreign nation. (4:3).
Happy are we, O Israel, for we know what is pleasing to God. (4:4).
Take courage, my people, who perpetuate Israel’s name! (4:5).
It was not for destruction that you were sold to the nations, but you were handed over to your enemies because you angered God. (4:6).
For you provoked the one who made you by sacrificing to demons and not to God. (4:7).
You forgot the everlasting God, who brought you up, and you grieved Jerusalem, who reared you. (4:8).
For she saw the wrath that came upon you from God, and she said: “Listen, you neighbors of Zion; God has brought great sorrow upon me, (4:9).
for I have seen the exile of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them. (4:10).
With joy I nurtured them, but I sent them away with weeping and sorrow. (4:11).
Let no one rejoice over me, a widow and bereaved of many; I was left desolate because of the sins of my children, because they turned away from the law of God. (4:12).
They had no regard for his statutes; they did not walk in the ways of God’s commandments or tread the paths his righteousness showed them. (4:13).
Let the neighbors of Zion come; remember the capture of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them. (4:14).
For he brought a distant nation against them, a nation ruthless and of a strange language, which had no respect for the aged and no pity for a child. (4:15).
They led away the widow’s beloved sons and bereaved the lonely woman of her daughters. (4:16).
“But I, how can I help you? (4:17).
For he who brought these calamities will deliver you from the hand of your enemies. (4:18).
Go, my children, go, for I have been left desolate. (4:19).
I have taken off the robe of peace and put on sackcloth for my supplication; I will cry to the Everlasting all my days. (4:20).
“Take courage, my children, cry to God, and he will deliver you from the power and hand of the enemy. (4:21).
For I have put my hope in the Everlasting to save you, and joy has come to me from the Holy One, because of the mercy that will soon come to you from your everlasting savior. (4:22).
For I sent you out with sorrow and weeping, but God will give you back to me with joy and gladness forever. (4:23).
For as the neighbors of Zion have now seen your capture, so they soon will see your salvation by God, which will come to you with great glory and with the splendor of the Everlasting. (4:24).
My children, endure with patience the wrath that has come upon you from God. Your enemy has overtaken you, but you will soon see their destruction and will tread upon their necks. (4:25).
My pampered children have traveled rough roads; they were taken away like a flock carried off by the enemy. (4:26).
“Take courage, my children, and cry to God, for you will be remembered by the one who brought this upon you. (4:27).
For just as you were disposed to go astray from God, return with tenfold zeal to seek him. (4:28).
For the one who brought these calamities upon you will bring you everlasting joy with your salvation.” (4:29).
Take courage, O Jerusalem, for the one who named you will comfort you. (4:30).
Wretched will be those who mistreated you and who rejoiced at your fall. (4:31).
Wretched will be the cities that your children served as slaves; wretched will be the city that received your offspring. (4:32).
For just as she rejoiced at your fall and was glad for your ruin, so she will be grieved at her own desolation. (4:33).
I will take away her pride in her great population, and her insolence will be turned to grief. (4:34).
For fire will come upon her from the Everlasting for many days, and for a long time she will be inhabited by demons. (4:35).
Look toward the east, O Jerusalem, and see the joy that is coming to you from God. (4:36).
Look, your children are coming, whom you sent away; they are coming, gathered from east and west, at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God. (4:37).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 32:16-17: They sacrificed to demons, not to God, to gods they had never known.
Lamentations 1:1: The city that was full of people now sits as a widow.
Deuteronomy 28:49-50: A distant nation of a strange language, showing no respect to the old and no mercy to the young.
Isaiah 47:8-9: The queen city that said she would never sit as a widow is left childless in one day.
Isaiah 49:18-22: Zion lifts her eyes and sees her children gathered and carried home to her.

translationNotes.note: Coarse dark cloth woven from goat hair and worn next to the skin so that it chafed. Putting it on in place of the robe of peace, meaning ordinary good clothing, was a visible public sign of mourning or petition.

In the Greek Old Testament daimonia renders the Hebrew shedim, the beings behind pagan sacrifice in Deuteronomy 32:17. The same Greek word also translates the terms for creatures said to occupy ruined and abandoned cities.
A widow had no legal standing of her own and no income unless a male relative acted for her. Calling Jerusalem a widow describes destitution and loss of legal protection, not grief alone.
The victor's formal gesture after a battle was to set a foot on the neck of the defeated, as Joshua's commanders do in Joshua 10:24. It signals conquest completed, not casual trampling.

stories.keyTakeaway: Wisdom is the book of God's commandments, the law that endures forever. Israel was handed over for sacrificing to demons, not for destruction. Jerusalem speaks as a widow in sackcloth, tells her children to take courage, curses the city that took them, and looks east to see them coming home.

stories.title: 📜 Baruch 5
summaryBullets: Take off the garment of your sorrow and affliction, O Jerusalem, and put on forever the beauty of the glory from God. (5:1).
Put on the robe of the righteousness that comes from God; put on your head the diadem of the glory of the Everlasting, (5:2).
for God will show your splendor everywhere under heaven, (5:3).
for God will give you evermore the name, “Righteous Peace, Godly Glory.” (5:4).
Arise, O Jerusalem, stand upon the height; look toward the east, and see your children gathered from west and east at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God has remembered them. (5:5).
For they went out from you on foot, led away by their enemies, but God will bring them back to you, carried in glory, as on a royal throne. (5:6).
For God has ordered that every high mountain and the everlasting hills be made low and the valleys filled up, to make level ground, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God. (5:7).
The woods and every fragrant tree have shaded Israel at God’s command. (5:8).
For God will lead Israel with joy, in the light of his glory, with the mercy and righteousness that come from him. (5:9).
crossRefs: Isaiah 52:1-2: Zion is told to put on strength and her beautiful garments, shake off the dust, and rise.
Isaiah 40:3-5: Every valley lifted and every mountain made low, so that the glory of the Lord is revealed.
Isaiah 62:2-4: Jerusalem is given a new name spoken by the mouth of the Lord.
Isaiah 60:4-5: Lift up your eyes and see; your sons come from far away and your daughters are carried.
Psalm 147:2-3: The Lord builds up Jerusalem and gathers the outcasts of Israel.

translationNotes.note: A heavy outer cloak folded double and worn over the shoulders. It was the garment of rank and public honor, the opposite of the plain mourning dress it replaces here.
A band of cloth wound around the head, worn by priests and people of rank. It is a wrapped headpiece, not the rigid jeweled crown a modern reader pictures.

translationNotes.original: Greek: εἰρήνη δικαιοσύνης καὶ δόξα θεοσεβείας (eirene dikaiosynes kai doxa theosebeias)
translationNotes.note: Literally the peace of righteousness and the glory of reverence for God. Theosebeia is the ordinary Greek word for piety, the practice of honoring God, so the new name describes a settled condition rather than a title of office.

translationNotes.original: Greek: στολὴ τοῦ πένθους (stole tou penthous)
translationNotes.note: A stole is a long formal robe. Mourning dress was a defined outfit worn for a set period, not merely drab clothes, so taking it off marks a public and deliberate end to the mourning.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jerusalem is told to take off the garment of sorrow, put on the robe of righteousness and the diadem of glory, and take the name Righteous Peace, Godly Glory. She stands on the height and sees her children carried home from west and east as God levels the mountains and fills the valleys.
